approximations: official map = log(C x PHOTMJSR) with C = rate SCI / cal SCI; it includes everything calwebb_image2 divides by besides PHOTMJSR, i.e. the flat reference file (pixel-to-pixel QE and the large-scale response); its smooth part is removed by the gauge projection anyway
pixels where C is rejected (non-finite, zero, or C x PHOTMJSR outside [0.2, 5]) are left out of every statistic

noise limit = 1 / sqrt(I_p): the Cramer-Rao bound of log G_p if the sky and all other terms were known exactly and the model mean equals the data; the sky is fitted from the same data (each sky position is seen by about as many exposures as each pixel), which inflates the variance by roughly N / (N - 1) (reported as 'noise_limit_inflated', N = median number of training exposures per filter of the detector, since each sky position is seen by about that many); kernel and sky-model errors near bright sources are not in it

with --ref-state (no gain map yet) the footprint is a 22.48-arcsec square per training exposure (data region) centred on its cut rectangle and rotated by the stored mean rotation (pixel scale 0.0311 / 0.0630 arcsec), ignoring distortion and the learned shifts (1-2 pixel errors at the edges); I_p = sum over training exposures covering p of (bkg0 / sigbar)^2 (background only: a lower bound where sources are)

detector mode with several filters: truth = information-weighted mean of the per-filter maps (the learned map is one map for all filters; its best constant-in-filter approximation of filter-dependent flats is this weighted mean only if the information is spread evenly)
label: NRCBLONG
